parts.label: Part 4
parts.article:
Part four.

You will hear part of a lecture about a marine creature called the red sea urchin.

First, you have some time to look at questions thirty-one to forty.

Now listen carefully and answer questions thirty-one to forty.

Good morning.

Last week, I talked about various research methods in the natural sciences, and you did some background reading on that topic. Today, I want to take up that theme again and look at a specific example of how data gained using newer techniques has really pushed our knowledge forward, more or less overturning existing theories.

So I'm going to look at the case of the red sea urchin.

First of all, some background. As the name suggests, this is a marine animal, and it's found in shallow coastal waters. It grazes on plants. It's an herbivore, in other words.

Here in North America, we can find it all along our West Coast, from Alaska down to California. So many of you will be familiar with it, and it survives very well because it's covered in spines, which are very sharp, and these deter most predators.

Now, in the nineteen sixties in this country, the sea urchin was thought to be partly responsible for the sudden decline in kelp, a plant which supports an extensive ecosystem. So in fact, it was considered to be a pest. Incidentally, since the nineteen sixties, the thinking on that has changed, and humans are now thought to be to blame. But anyway, red sea urchins weren't popular, and people even tried to poison them to get rid of them in any way possible.

But then in the nineteen seventies, attitudes changed.

Interestingly, this had nothing to do with science. There were no new insights into the biology of the sea urchin. It was, in fact, a purely economic development. It became apparent that there was a demand for the red sea urchin in Asia, where certain parts of the animal were considered to be a great delicacy. And so a commercial fishery was established based on sea urchins. They brought high prices. In fact, at one point during the nineteen nineties, they were one of the most valuable marine resources in the state of California.

So people began to look at the sea urchin in a different light. And just at this time, people noticed an apparent decline in the numbers of sea urchins. This prompted a wave of scientific studies with the purpose of getting more information about the species, its life cycle, its biology, survival rate, growth patterns, and so on.

So what did research uncover? Well, the most significant findings came from research based on biochemical techniques.

Basically, individual sea urchins were tagged and injected with tetracycline, which allowed researchers to track their growth rates.

And it quickly became apparent that the sea urchins grew a lot more slowly and lived a lot longer than had previously been thought. Astonishingly, they can have a vast lifespan greater than that of almost any other terrestrial or marine species. They can live to be one hundred years old, and some may even reach two hundred. Just imagine, an individual red sea urchin that hatched early in the nineteenth century may still be thriving and even breeding.

It was found that this animal does grow fairly quickly when it's young. At the age of two, it can grow from two to four centimeters in just one year. But even then, according to scientists who conducted the research, it still takes six or seven years before it's big enough to be harvested. By the time the red sea urchin is a teenager, its growth slows quite dramatically. And from the age of twenty-two, when it's about twelve centimeters long, it grows at just point one of a centimeter a year.

But somehow, the animal never really stops growing. It just grows incredibly slowly.

Some of the largest and probably the oldest sea urchins were found off the coast of British Columbia between Vancouver Island and the mainland.

And now another very recent study, one using an entirely different technique, has produced independent evidence for these findings. The study measured levels of radiocarbon, and it has shown that even very old sea urchins show almost no sign of aging when something finally kills them.

Unlike when someone looks at you or me, you can't look at a sea urchin and say whether it's young or middle-aged. And in addition to that, even when they're incredibly ancient, they are still able to breed.

So by now, you may be wondering how with this phenomenal lifespan, there aren't a lot more sea urchins around than there actually are. Well, there is a suggestion that reproduction rates for the species are low because not many red sea urchins are able to survive the first year of life.

The study also confirmed the finding that in older sea urchins, there is a very steady, very consistent rate of growth, and this growth is independent of ocean conditions and other variables.

So what are the implications of these findings?

That is the end of Part four. You now have one minute to check your answers to Part four.

analyses.content: 录音中明确提到海胆“grazes on plants”（以植物为食），这里的 graze on 完美对应题干的 feeds on。
你可能会听到紧随其后的 herbivore（食草动物），但题目需要填的是它具体“吃什么”而不是“它是什么动物”，且填 herbivore 也不如 plants 直接。
It grazes on plants. It's an herbivore, in other words.
录音提到它能很好地存活是因为“covered in spines”（长满尖刺），这直接点出了起保护作用的覆盖物。
千万不要因为听到了后面的 predators（捕食者）就填进去，录音说的是尖刺能“震慑”（deter）捕食者，捕食者是防御对象而非它身上的东西。
And it survives very well because it's covered in spines, which are very sharp, and these deter most predators.
录音里原话总结说“it was considered to be a pest”（它被认为是一种害虫），这里的 considered to be 直接同义替换了题干的 regarded as。
前面出现的 kelp（海带）是一个强干扰，但那是海胆导致数量减少的植物，并不是海胆本身被赋予的称呼。

Now, in the nineteen sixties, in this country, the sea urchin was thought to be partly responsible for the sudden decline in kelp, a plant which supports an extensive ecosystem. So in fact, it was considered to be a pest.
听到“became apparent”和表示需求的“demand”后，紧接着定位到的地点就是“in Asia”（在亚洲），对应题目的重要市场（important market）。
你可能会被前面提及的 economic development 干扰，但这只是交代大背景，真正的市场区域词只有 Asia。
It was, in fact, a purely economic development. It became apparent that there was a demand for the red sea urchin in Asia, where certain parts of the animal were considered to be a great delicacy.
录音指出人们注意到海胆数量出现了明显的“decline”（下降），这促发了一波科学研究（prompted a wave of scientific studies），对应题干的科学兴趣增加。
不要单填 numbers，题目问的是种群数量发生了“什么”变化导致了研究，填“下降”才符合完整逻辑。

And just at this time, people noticed an apparent decline in the numbers of sea urchins. This prompted a wave of scientific studies with the purpose of getting more information about the species, its life cycle, its biology, survival rate, growth patterns, and so on.
录音提到它们能活到100岁，随后补充说有些甚至能达到（reach）两百岁（two hundred），这才是题目要求的最大寿命（maximum life span）。

注意，不能填“200 years old”。题干里的“寿命长达……”后面问的是“多长时间”（200 年），而“200 years old”意思是“200 岁”，英语里不能说“寿命长达 200 岁”，只能说“寿命长达 200 年（200 years）”。另外，极容易听到 one hundred years old 就赶紧写上，忽略了题干中 maximum（最大）这个限定词，一定要听完句子的后半部分转折或递进。

They can live to be one hundred years old, and some may even reach two hundred. Just imagine, an individual red sea urchin that hatched early in the nineteenth century may still be thriving and even breeding.
录音里明确指出，从22岁开始，它每年仅仅生长“point one of a centimeter”（0.1厘米）。英文的单位是：只要前面的数字不是 1，单位就必须加 s，除非你写成0.1cm.
前面抛出的 twelve centimeters（12厘米）是个巨大的陷阱，那是它22岁时的“总身长”，而不是题干所问的“每年生长量”。
And from the age of twenty-two, when it's about twelve centimeters long, it grows at just point one of a centimeter a year.
录音明确指出，即使是很老的海胆在死时也几乎没有“aging”（衰老）的迹象（no sign of），这里的 no sign of 直接替换了题干的 no evidence of。
有些同学可能会试图拼写 radiocarbon，但那是研究测量的手段，而不是海胆死亡时缺乏的“证据”。
The study measured levels of radiocarbon, and it has shown that even very old sea urchins show almost no sign of aging when something finally kills them.
录音提到，哪怕它们已经极其古老（incredibly ancient = very old），它们仍然能够“breed”（繁殖）。
跟丢的同学可能会觉得 ancient 不是 old，但其实就是 very old 的同义替换，死死盯住“still able to”就能抓出动作 breed。
And in addition to that, even when they're incredibly ancient, they are still able to breed.
录音结尾总结这种生长独立于（independent of）“ocean conditions”（海洋条件）和其他变量，independent of 就是 not connected to 的直接替换。
很容易只填 ocean 或者只填 conditions，要注意听完整这个名词短语，少字会导致意思不精确而被扣分。
The study also confirmed the finding that in older sea urchins, there is a very steady, very consistent rate of growth, and this growth is independent of ocean conditions and other variables.
